copyright_policy: Transfer timing, density, handoff structure, and dialogue-placement patterns only. Never copy sentences, jokes, titles, or distinctive channel wording.

references.analysis_basis: Korean automatic captions merged with 0.08-second tolerance
references.limitations: Caption-free windows may contain movie dialogue, reactions, action, music, or effects and are not literal silence.

references.analysis_basis: Original Korean automatic captions merged with 0.08-second tolerance
references.limitations: Coverage includes reviewer narration and Korean movie dialogue, so it measures spoken-flow continuity rather than narration share.

references.profile: same-film reference: narration-led with saved dialogue blocks
references.analysis_basis: Korean automatic captions merged with 0.08-second tolerance, then split by script: Hangul blocks are the reviewer, Latin blocks are the film's own dialogue left in place
references.limitations: Reviews the same film as our project and includes the ending, which our spoiler rule forbids carrying over. Caption-free windows are not silence.

rules.instruction: Use a denser short hook, let strong original dialogue carry the middle, and return to concise urgency only during the pre-resolution climb.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if the middle becomes causally unclear or the hook narrates future results.

rules.instruction: Use one short setup, then return to a meaningful movie line or reaction before adding another bridge.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if narration repeats the next movie line or three narration blocks become consecutive.

rules.instruction: Use rapid narration-dialogue handoffs only when short original lines deliver an answer, threat, retort, or emotional response; otherwise compress the scene.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if speaker changes become confusing or emotional residue is cut off.

rules.instruction: Choose long original-audio breathing, micro-interleaving, or protected no-narration per story unit; never average reference densities into one global narration rate.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if a discovery, reversal, death, confession, horror payoff, or action payoff receives added narration.

rules.instruction: Keep narration blocks near 6 seconds and place one roughly every 18 seconds, leaving about 6.5 seconds of film between them. Fix spacing, not block length.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if bridges start narrating what the next line already says, if three narration blocks land consecutively, or if a protected scene gains narration.
rules.measurement: Reference: 61 narration blocks over 1085 s, block median 6.00 s, gap median 6.56 s, cycle 17.8 s. Constantine V5: 29 blocks over 1501 s, block median 5.90 s, gap median 15.72 s, cycle 51.8 s. Block length already matched; the cycle was 2.9x too long.

rules.instruction: Aim for the reviewer's own narration to cover about 40 percent of the runtime, and keep roughly 10 percent as the film's own dialogue left audible. Treat a narration share under 25 percent as a structural fault.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if reaching the share requires narrating over strong dialogue, restating movie lines, or filling protected scenes.
rules.measurement: Reference: narration 41.9 percent, kept film dialogue 10.2 percent, 54.2 percent of the runtime carrying some speech. Constantine V5 narration 11.0 percent. An earlier reading of 54.2 percent as narration was wrong: it counted the film's own English lines as narration.

rules.instruction: Open dense, thin through the middle, and come back up for the final stretch.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if the thinned middle loses causal clarity or the dense opening reveals a future result.
rules.measurement: Reference narration by 5-minute window: 51.8, 40.5, 27.6, 50.9 percent. The dip is deeper than first measured and lands in the third quarter, where the reference hands long stretches to the film's own confrontation dialogue.

rules.instruction: Target 17 to 19 minutes. The reference covers the same 139-minute film in 18.1.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if required story events or causal links have to be dropped to hit the length.
rules.measurement: Reference 18.1 minutes for a 138.9-minute film. Constantine V5 used 25.0 minutes and 20.5 percent of its source.

rules.instruction: Leave the film's own dialogue audible in a few long blocks at the confrontations, not sprinkled evenly. Around ten blocks of roughly 10 seconds each.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if a kept block runs without narration long enough to lose the thread, or if it reveals a result the script has not reached yet.
rules.measurement: Reference keeps 10 dialogue blocks, median 10.0 s, longest 22.3 s, clustered at 1:38, 11:28-12:17 and 15:46-16:13 — the preacher scene and the two confrontations.

rules.instruction: Show the final confrontation in full and cut on the last line before the outcome. Do not stop short of the confrontation itself, and do not cross into its result.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if the cut point lands after any line or image that states who survives, or if it lands so early that the two sides never face each other on screen.
rules.measurement: The film's subtitles stop at 7564.42 s and resume at 7615.08 s; that 50-second gap is the shootout. 7615 is already the loser dying and 7644 states the outcome. Cutting at 7570 keeps both guns raised. An earlier draft cut at 7380, which removed the confrontation altogether and cost the climax.

rules.instruction: Close on one unbroken block: the theme in a single line, then how to read the protagonist, then the cast, then an invitation to watch. Promise the cast in the title and pay it off only here.
rules.rollback_condition: Reject if the closing block states the outcome, or if the cast hook is spent early enough that nothing is left to hold the viewer.
rules.measurement: The reference's final block runs 66.5 s unbroken and carries theme, protagonist reading, cast, and a viewing note in that order. Its title hook is the cast, and it is only named at 16:51 of an 18:05 video.
